one_line: Karan administrator of Rajamahendri and Vaishnava dramatist at the Gajapati court.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his late 30s to early 40s, medium height, slightly sturdy build with a composed, disciplined posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a calm, wheat-brown complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed black mustache, soft but focused large anime-style eyes with a thoughtful gaze, a small vertical sandalwood tilaka on the forehead, and a default expression of gentle, contemplative seriousness that can turn into a warm, knowing smile.
appearance.hair: Glossy black hair pulled back into a modest, neatly tied knot at the back of the head (not a high topknot), with a simple narrow off-white cloth band tied around the crown like a subtle headscarf-strip, leaving the forehead clear.
appearance.costume: Era-accurate late-15th–early-16th-century eastern Deccan/Coastal Odisha-Andhra attire: a long, finely woven off-white cotton upper cloth (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and wrapped snugly around the torso, covering the chest fully, with a light cream tinge and a thin golden-yellow woven border; below, a ankle-length plain white cotton dhoti with a slightly thicker golden-yellow border, pleated in front and wrapped securely around the waist; the waist is encircled by a narrow reddish-brown cloth belt, and he wears simple brown leather sandals; his right wrist bears a single wooden bead bracelet, and he has small, plain gold stud earrings; the overall textile look is clean, crisp, and unornamented, with very subtle striping in the dhoti fabric to show fine weaving but no heavy patterns.
appearance.signature: A neatly rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord held in his left hand, with one partially unrolled palm leaf and a slender metal stylus tucked into the cord, symbolizing both his administrative documentation and dramatic writing.

ref_desc: Ramananda Ray is a wheat-brown, oval-faced man in his late 30s–40s with a neat black hair-knot, small tilaka, off-white uttariya, white dhoti with golden-yellow borders, reddish-brown waist cloth, simple sandals, and a rolled palm-leaf manuscript with stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Ramananda Ray, a dignified late-15th–early-16th-century Karan administrator from the Godavari–Puri region: he appears in his late 30s–40s, medium height with a slightly sturdy build and calm posture, wheat-brown complexion, an oval face, straight nose, neatly trimmed black mustache, and large thoughtful eyes with a gentle but serious default expression and a small vertical sandalwood tilaka on his forehead. His glossy black hair is pulled back into a modest, low knot at the back of the head, with a simple narrow off-white cloth band tied around the crown, leaving the forehead clear. He wears a finely woven off-white cotton uttariya draped over both shoulders and wrapped to cover his torso completely, with a thin golden-yellow border, and a full-length white cotton dhoti with slightly thicker golden-yellow borders, neatly pleated and wrapped to the ankles. A narrow reddish-brown cloth belt is tied around his waist, he has small plain gold stud earrings, a single wooden bead bracelet on his right wrist, and simple brown leather sandals. In his left hand he holds his signature prop: a rolled palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a red cord, one leaf partly unrolled and a slender metal stylus tucked into the cord. Use a restrained palette of off-white, white, golden yellow, reddish brown, and brown, and present him from multiple angles to clearly show his consistent face, hair knot with cloth band, draped garments, borders, sandals, and palm-leaf manuscript with stylus.
